hints: Multiply through by $\cos^2\theta$ to clear all denominators.
Apply $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ and rearrange into a quadratic in $\sin\theta$.
walkthrough:
Multiply through by $\cos^2\theta$ to clear fractions:
$$7\sin\theta + 12\cos^2\theta = 0$$

Multiply by $-1$ and rearrange terms in descending powers:
$$12\sin^2\theta - 7\sin\theta - 12 = 0$$

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Uses $\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ to get $\frac{7\sin\theta}{\cos^2\theta}+12=0$ (M1). Applies $\cos^2\theta = 1-\sin^2\theta$ (DM1). Concludes correctly with $12\sin^2\theta-7\sin\theta-12=0$ (A1).

hints: Solve for $\sin\theta$, rejecting any solution outside $[-1, 1]$.
Solve $\sin\theta = -\frac{3}{4}$ for all values of $\theta$ in $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Solve for $\sin\theta$, rejecting values outside the valid range $[-1, 1]$:
$$\sin\theta = -\frac{3}{4} \quad \text{or} \quad \sin\theta = \frac{4}{3} \quad (\text{reject since } \frac{4}{3} > 1)$$

Find the reference angle and quadrant solutions for $\sin\theta = -0.75$ in $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\text{Reference angle: } \alpha = \arcsin(0.75) \approx 48.59^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant III: } \theta = 180^\circ + 48.59^\circ = 228.6^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant IV: } \theta = 360^\circ - 48.59^\circ = 311.4^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Factorises the quadratic to $(4\sin\theta+3)(3\sin\theta-4)=0$ (M1). Obtains $\sin\theta = -\frac{3}{4}$ (B1). Finds both solutions $\theta = 228.6^\circ, 311.4^\circ$ with no extras in range (B1).
